gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: 20 original sentences covering completed actions, sequences, past habits, negatives, and questions — always with a clear finished-time marker, never a present-perfect one.

questions.explain: A finished action at a specific past time: last Saturday.
'Yesterday morning' — a clear, finished time in the past.
'Buy' is irregular: buy → bought.
'Leave' is irregular: leave → left.
Short verb ending in a single consonant: double it before -ed — cancelled.
One completed event following another — plain past simple, no 'while' or 'when' needed.

questions.before: He finished his homework, and then he
questions.explain: 'Then' links two completed actions, one after the other.
'Get' is irregular: get → got.

questions.after: a bike to school every day.
questions.explain: A repeated habit that's now over — past simple, not present.

questions.after: football every weekend when we were kids.
questions.explain: 'Every weekend' describes a past routine, now finished.
A state that was true in the past but no longer is.

questions.after: in this town his whole life.
questions.explain: A past state, now finished (implies he no longer does).

questions.after: hard for every test at school.
questions.explain: Consonant + y → change y to i before adding -ed: studied.
Negative past simple: didn't + base verb.
After 'didn't', the verb goes back to its base form: go, not went.
'Didn't' + base verb — never 'didn't finished'.
Negative past simple with the base form: catch, not caught.
Past simple questions always start with 'did', whatever the subject.
'Did' + subject + base verb — the main verb stays uninflected.
A simple yes/no question about a finished event.
